items: Liquids diffuse like gases, but the rate of diffusion in liquids is much lower.
There is little space among liquid molecules because of relatively stronger intermolecular forces.
Liquids are 10^5 times less compressible than gases but about 10 times more compressible than solids.
The molecules of a liquid are in constant random motion, but slower than in gases. Diffusion among miscible liquids is evidence of this free motion, and liquids flow because of it.
Liquids expand when heated, but the expansion is negligible compared with that of gases.

By the kinetic molecular theory the molecules of a liquid are in constant motion and so possess kinetic energy at any temperature; it rises or falls with the temperature. A liquid becomes a solid when its kinetic energy is decreased (cooling) and a vapour when it is increased (heating).

blocks.prompt: Two miscible liquids are poured carefully into one beaker and left; after a time they are evenly mixed without stirring. Which property of liquids does this show, and why is it slower than the same process in gases?
blocks.explanation: It shows diffusion, which comes from the constant random motion of liquid molecules. It is slower than in gases because liquid molecules are close together with little space between them and move more slowly, held by stronger intermolecular forces.

items: Liquids diffuse (slowly), have little space between molecules, are 10^5 times less compressible than gases and 10 times more than solids, flow by random motion, expand only slightly, and change state as their kinetic energy falls (to solid) or rises (to vapour).
